standard_prerequisites.name: The relation a^N x y = 0 in the blowup algebra for large N
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts vanishing of a product in R[I/a] into an honest product relation in R, where domain-ness can be applied.

core_obligations: Write two arbitrary elements of R[I/a] as x/a^n and y/a^m with x in I^n and y in I^m (proof lines 17546-17547).
Assume their product is zero and pull the relation back to R, obtaining a^N x y = 0 in R for some N (proof line 17548).
Use that R is a domain and that a is nonzero to conclude that one of x, y is zero, so one of the two elements vanishes in the blowup algebra (proof lines 17548-17549).
proof_roadmap: Put two elements into the standard fractional form x/a^n, y/a^m taken from the description of the blowup algebra (proof lines 17545-17547).
Clear denominators to reach a^N x y = 0 in the domain R and conclude that a factor vanishes (proof lines 17548-17550).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a domain R, an ideal I and a nonzero element a of I, the affine blowup algebra R[I/a] is again a domain (statement lines 17539-17543). The proof does not construct an embedding of R[I/a] into a known domain: it takes two general elements in the fractional form x/a^n and y/a^m supplied by the description of the blowup algebra, clears denominators to reach the relation a^N x y = 0 in R, and uses that R is a domain together with a being nonzero to kill a factor (proof lines 17545-17550). The clearing of denominators, which is what converts a vanishing product in the blowup algebra into a statement about R, is the step that carries the content. H2.
